props.text: Point a coding agent (Copilot, Claude, Cursor …) at this running instance so the workforce's operations become native tools — submit work, answer escalations, read status, and debug a wedged instance without curl. The Urban runtime serves a Streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint for this app at the /app/mcp path — behind a reverse-proxy prefix the reachable URL carries that prefix, as the recipes below render — and projects its openapi.yaml into tools, with zero MCP code in nwf. Register ONE server entry per instance; its tools are namespaced under the name you give it, so naming the instance targets the right one and makes the wrong-instance mistake very hard to hit (a server pointed at the wrong URL can still misfire). Use the copyable recipes below — each URL is already rendered for THIS instance's address (including any reverse-proxy prefix).

modal.title: One server entry per instance
modal.description: Add to ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json (user-wide) or .mcp.json (repo-scoped). The workforce-local entry is pre-filled with THIS instance's URL; the merlin/remote entries show the LAN and ngrok shapes — give each node its own named entry. If THIS instance is guarded (NANO_PR_WEBHOOK_SECRET set), add the same "headers": { "x-hook-secret": "$NANO_PR_WEBHOOK_SECRET" } block to workforce-local too, or its calls 401. MCP servers register at host startup, so add the entry, THEN start a new session for its tools to load.

modal.title: Add from the terminal
modal.description: For a guarded instance (NANO_PR_WEBHOOK_SECRET set), pass the shared-secret header with the --header form (the second command); an unguarded instance needs only the first.
modal.copyText:
# This instance if unguarded (no NANO_PR_WEBHOOK_SECRET set):
copilot mcp add --transport http workforce-local {{appBase}}app/mcp

# This instance if guarded (NANO_PR_WEBHOOK_SECRET set) — present the shared secret header:
copilot mcp add --transport http workforce-local {{appBase}}app/mcp \
  --header "x-hook-secret: $NANO_PR_WEBHOOK_SECRET"

props.text: When this instance sets NANO_PR_WEBHOOK_SECRET, the guard is NOT mutation-only — it also covers reads, so read endpoints like GET /app/api/agent and GET /app/api/version return 401 without the x-hook-secret header, just as guarded mutations do. It is not blanket, though: a few doors stay intentionally unguarded even when the secret is set (e.g. the declarative Save-to-library page action, which structurally cannot attach the header). The mcp-config.json path takes the shared secret as a headers block, not a flag, so add a headers block alongside url on the server entry (copy it below); omitting it yields 401s. Put the secret in the server entry's headers, never in chat. When NANO_PR_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, the app guard is off entirely — reads and mutations both work with no credential from wherever this instance is reachable (with network.bind "all" that is the LAN, not just loopback), so unset it only where that exposure is acceptable. Note the runtime-served /app/mcp surface is an exception to that reachability: it is loopback-only by default and refuses non-loopback peers with a 403 even when network.bind is "all", until you also set URBAN_MCP_ALLOW_REMOTE=true — LAN/remote MCP clients need that knob in addition to a wide bind.

modal.title: Add the x-hook-secret header
modal.description: Drop this headers entry alongside url on the guarded server's config-form entry.

props.text: These are two different layers. x-hook-secret is the app's own guard, checked by nwf. Basic Auth is enforced by whatever fronts the instance (ngrok edge, console proxy) and 401s before the request ever reaches nwf. A Basic-Auth-fronted instance therefore needs BOTH headers on the connection: Authorization: Basic … for the proxy AND x-hook-secret for the app. Generate the blob with printf '%s' 'user:pass' | base64 (echo appends a newline and yields the wrong value); Base64 is encoding, not encryption — only use Basic Auth over HTTPS.

modal.title: Both headers, two different layers
modal.description: Proxy layer (Authorization) plus app layer (x-hook-secret) on the same server entry.

props.text: The framework's mutating engine-debug tools (set_variables / retry_job / resolve_incident / cancel_instance) require the app's shared-secret scheme (or the loopback-only allowMutations opt-in when allowRemote is off). Until issue #698 declares x-nano-secret-env, remote mutations are refused on any allowRemote-on instance even with reads open — that is the current posture, tracked in #698. The read tools (urban_debug_search_process_instances / _element_instance_wait_states / _incidents, and where projected _jobs / _variables) work under the same x-hook-secret as the rest of the surface. Operator-only doors stay operator-only: the delivery-graph stage / dispatch / dismiss lifecycle is x-mcp-excluded from the tool surface — the human clicking Dispatch in the cockpit IS the approval — so an agent cannot dispatch a delivery graph through MCP (it authors graphs through the pure compileDeliveryGraph / previewDeliveryGraph doors, which stay exposed).

Agents without an MCP client are unchanged — fetch and follow this instance's live operator guide over curl (the response is JSON with a skill markdown field). Add -H "x-hook-secret: <secret>" (and -u user:pass for a Basic-Auth-fronted instance) if this instance is guarded. That skill bootstraps you to the same live guide MCP exposes as the getAgentInstructions tool — or, over MCP, its addressable companion getAgentGuide(section?), which the runbook recommends over the ~43KB blob to avoid a tool-result overrun.

modal.title: The curl door is unchanged
modal.description: Fetch this instance's live guide directly; add the header(s) if guarded.
modal.copyText:
curl -sS {{appBase}}app/api/agent/skill
# guarded instance — add the shared secret (and Basic Auth if fronted):
curl -sS {{appBase}}app/api/agent/skill \
  -H "x-hook-secret: <secret>"
